evidence.entryPriority: Search and shortage-only control directly precede the inventory. SKU, location and explicit '8 pieces shortage' make LIN-115 distinguishable without selection; desktop Inspect is at y454. The large disclosure and heading delay mobile inventory, but LIN-115 Inspect remains in the original first viewport at y731.
evidence.decisionContext: Desktop review keeps the selected row beside the full item name and six explicitly labeled evidence cells: available 2, reorder 10, shortage 8, incoming 4, B-04 and pieces. Requested 8 pieces and the no-purchase-order notice immediately precede Edit quantity and Save decision. Repeated item/shortage/location information consumes space without adding relationships.
evidence.narrowContext: Mobile preserves search, filter and the selected inventory card above detail, and the full long name wraps rather than disappearing. Two-column metrics remain readable. However the repeated stock evidence and long header put original review actions at y1754, requiring substantial travel between retained list and decision. 320px geometry reports no horizontal overflow, which does not remove this scrolling burden.
evidence.recoveryFlow: The mobile failure visibly names a simulated save error, retains LIN-115 and pending 8 pieces, and places Retry decision beside Edit quantity. Error is below the full stock evidence, so it is not immediate on entering the stacked detail. Scripted traces on both viewports confirm invalid values rejected, edit retains quantity, failure retains state, retry records the simulation, and return retains search/filter; these passes establish behavior rather than ease.
evidence.compositionPurpose: The familiar list/detail split supports comparing the selected evidence and review on desktop. Shortage labels use words and quantities, not only color. Yet the large empty-state instruction panel, nested metric cards and repeated selected-item badges make a five-item task unnecessarily tall, especially when stacked on mobile.

blockers: No task-completion blocker observed. Separate accessibility finding: axe reports 4.35:1 contrast for current-shortage label/unit in failure and final states on both viewports, below its 4.5:1 threshold.
unnecessaryRegions: The empty detail panel repeats selection instructions and simulation disclosure already present above.
A dedicated inventory-unit tile and repeated location/shortage badges add vertical space when units and location already appear alongside values.
samples.genericityNote: Conventional bordered list/detail panels and nested metric cards remain. The split itself is task-fit; the less purposeful part is duplicating inventory evidence across the selected row, detail header, evidence grid and review rather than using the space to shorten the decision path.
samples.monochromeCaveat: Monochrome removes colored shortage/selected-state cues but retains textual labels and borders. Long-name wrapping and the mobile inventory-count/filter wrap also occur in authored images, so those are not inferred solely from font replacement. Geometry judgments use the original packet values, not transformed image measurements.

evidence.entryPriority: Desktop table puts all five items and their quantities in a compact comparable area (54px rows; LIN-115 Inspect at y289). Search/filter are adjacent above it. However SHORTAGE displays -8 while the task fixture and later summary use positive 8, adding interpretation. Mobile has a large blank gap between search and filter, and LIN-115 Inspect is originally at y1049, below the first viewport.
evidence.decisionContext: Review retains the selected row and summarizes the full LIN-115 name, B-04, available 2, shortage 8, incoming 4, requested 8 pieces and no-purchase-order consequence. Reorder 10 remains in the selected row rather than in the summary, separating part of the justification. The narrow desktop detail column wraps long item and stock-status strings, while list -8 and summary 8 use inconsistent shortage presentation.
evidence.narrowContext: Mobile retains list state and all named evidence without document horizontal overflow, including at 320px. But each table row becomes about 311px of single-column lines, a large blank filter region persists in the authored capture, and selected detail begins only below the card. The primary item's initial action at y1049 and review Save at y1275 show the cost despite successful scripted completion.
evidence.recoveryFlow: Mobile 'Save Interrupted' and 'Save Failed (Simulated)' explicitly say LIN-115 and 8 pieces were preserved. The summary, no-order disclosure and full-width Retry/Edit/Back actions make the next action understandable. The scripted traces confirm retry success, retained quantity, valid edits and retained search/filter on return. They do not establish discoverability or keyboard ease.
evidence.compositionPurpose: Desktop table efficiently aligns available/reorder/shortage/incoming across all items, a useful familiar pattern. The right review uses much less width than its wrapped content needs, while the empty instruction card and mobile one-field-per-line cards create avoidable space and travel.

blockers: No task-completion blocker observed. Separate accessibility findings: axe reports selected-row label/unit contrast of 4.37:1 in failure/final states; the inline Clear target is 43 by 17px with insufficient spacing for the reported 24px criterion.
unnecessaryRegions: Large empty space between mobile search and shortage filter appears in both authored full and failure captures.
The empty evidence panel repeats selection instructions, adds an example-SKU tip, and remains a large block after all five mobile rows.
Two Back to list controls in the compact review panel duplicate the same exit.
samples.genericityNote: The table/detail pattern is appropriate for inventory comparison and earns no penalty for familiarity. Generic nested summary/disclosure panels remain, with limited adaptation of column balance to the long item name and little purposeful use of mobile vertical space.
samples.monochromeCaveat: The monochrome diagnostic loses amber shortage and teal selection cues, but negative shortage tokens and selected labels remain. The blank mobile filter gap and tall cards persist in authored images, so they are supported layout observations. Desktop location wrapping appears more pronounced in monochrome; it is not treated as a separate failure.

comparison: Sample-2 makes desktop cross-item comparison faster through compact aligned rows, whereas sample-1 makes shortage meaning and each evidence quantity more explicit and gives desktop review more usable width. Both preserve list state and support a recoverable simulated decision in the supplied traces. Sample-1 has the clearer mobile metric grouping and earlier primary-item action; sample-2 has the more explicit preservation message and shorter failure summary path. Both retain substantial stacked-list scrolling, repeated instructions and conventional panel composition; neither is uniformly stronger across these task relationships.
limitations: Inspected the supplied 16 images only: for sample-1 then sample-2, four monochrome captures followed by four authored captures, each covering desktop full, mobile full, desktop review and mobile failure.

No live interaction was performed. No-results, quantity validation, edit and successful retry behavior are supported by supplied scripted observations rather than additional screenshots; passing checks do not prove ease or full accessibility conformance.

Original geometry and axe observations were read from packet.json. Full-page screenshots do not show scroll position, focus movement or how users discover offscreen feedback. 320px evidence is geometry only, with no supplied 320px image.
This single pair and the observed states do not support general model, condition or host rankings.
